We prove that, for every fixed $α>0$, $E_0(α,Λ)=(1+o(1))\,c_α\,α^{2/7}Λ^{12/7}$, with an explicit constant $c_α=0.99338\ldots$, as $Λ\to\infty$. The same asymptotics hold uniformly in the joint limit $Λ/α\to\infty$, $α^{5/2}Λ\to\infty$, provided $\log(2+α)=o((Λ/α)^{1/21})$. The infimum of the energy over product states has the same leading asymptotics. The upper bound follows from a coherent state bound for the field energy in a fixed electron density. For the lower bound we combine a periodization of the field, a blockwise Born-Oppenheimer bound, and a lower bound on the magnetic Neumann Laplacian on a cube for band-limited fields. The magnetic estimate follows from a non-concentration bound for the vorticity of band-limited fields satisfying a weighted gradient condition.

papers.title: Enhancing Type 2 Diabetes Diagnosis with Evolutionary Algorithms and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes is a widespread chronic disease that requires early and accurate diagnosis to prevent serious complications. Traditional diagnostic methods often lack sufficient accuracy, which highlights the need for more reliable computational solutions. In this study, we propose a model that integrates the Random Forest classifier with the Bat Optimization Algorithm for simultaneous feature selection and hyperparameter tuning. The SMOTE-ENN method was first applied to the Pima Indians Diabetes Database to correct class imbalance and remove noisy or ambiguous samples, producing a more balanced and cleaner dataset. The optimized model trained on this refined dataset achieved 89% accuracy, 88% precision, 90% recall, and an F1-score of 89%, clearly outperforming the baseline Random Forest and other existing approaches. These results demonstrate the potential of combining evolutionary algorithms with ensemble learning to provide a practical and cost-effective tool for early detection of type 2 diabetes in clinical practice.

papers.title: Decision-Native Recommendation with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) bring world knowledge to user preference modeling in sequential recommendation, but generation-based recommenders express next-item predictions indirectly as text. Generated outputs may fail to identify a unique candidate item, depend on candidate presentation order in the prompt, and lack explicit confidence in the recommendation. Recent studies explore Jev, a model for fast option selection with explicit confidence. Inspired by Jev, we introduce decision-native recommendation, a new paradigm that jointly models item choice and recommendation confidence using LLM representations. It requires valid candidate selection, consistency under candidate reordering, and confidence that reflects recommendation accuracy. We propose Direct Item Choice Estimation (DICE), which learns a personalized next-item distribution over supplied candidates from user interaction history and recommends the highest-scoring item with calibrated confidence. Tree-structured attention shares history computation across isolated candidate branches for order-consistent candidate scoring in a single forward pass. On three recommendation datasets, DICE achieves higher top-one accuracy than all evaluated baselines. Separate evaluations show unchanged item choices under tested candidate reorderings and end-to-end speedups of up to approximately $6\times$ over the evaluated generation-based methods. Its confidence estimates support selective recommendation by identifying more reliable predictions and guide additional computation for low-confidence examples in offline routing.

papers.title: The effective mass of the Pauli-Fierz electron: a cutoff-independent lower bound and the breakdown of mass renormalization
papers.abstract: We study the effective mass of a spinless non-relativistic electron coupled to the quantized transverse electromagnetic field (the Pauli-Fierz model without external potential), with bare mass $m$, fine structure constant $α=e^2/4π$ and a sharp ultraviolet cutoff $Λ$. We define $1/(2m_{\rm eff}):=\limsup_{P\to0}(E(P)-E(0))/|P|^2$ for the fiber ground state energy $E(P)$; this agrees with the curvature mass whenever $E$ is twice differentiable at zero. By scaling, $h=m_{\rm eff}/m$ depends only on $α$ and $λ=Λ/m$. For all $α>0$ and $λ\ge1$ we prove $h\ge1+0.3441\,α/(1+0.2985\sqrtα+0.1252\,α)$, a bound independent of the cutoff; with the band extended to the cutoff, its first order coefficient in $α$ is the perturbative one of Hiroshima and Spohn. At fixed $α>0$ we further prove $h\geλ^{8/7-ε}$ for every $ε>0$ and all sufficiently large $λ$. Hence $ι_{\rm PF}(α):=\inf_{λ>0}h/λ>0$: at fixed coupling, a bare mass reproducing a prescribed physical mass $m_{\rm phys}$ can exist only if $Λ\le m_{\rm phys}/ι_{\rm PF}(α)$. This proves the obstruction to mass renormalization at fixed physical mass anticipated by Lieb and Loss (2002). The first bound uses a coherent translation of the field applied to the ground state as a trial state. The second uses the sharp self-energy asymptotics of a companion paper and a position estimator constructed from the local centre of a shallow level set of the photon cloud.

papers.title: HumanoidNDM: Closing the Training-Deployment Gap of Motion Tracking via Humanoid Neural Dynamics Model
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots have recently achieved remarkable success in motion tracking. However, during real-world deployment, robots inevitably encounter dynamics gaps arising from either extra physical disturbances or inaccurate simulation modeling, resulting in a significant training-deployment gap. Therefore, effectively leveraging real-world data to fine-tune policies represents the crucial last mile for robust deployment. To bridge this gap, we propose HumanoidNDM, an online fine-tuning framework for humanoid motion tracking driven by a real-world-trained neural dynamics model. First, in the data collection stage, we introduce a low-frequency reference perturbation method with an adaptive intensity mechanism, balancing deployment feasibility and exploration efficiency. Second, for the model training stage, we train a robust history-based, proprioceptive neural dynamics model in Euclidean space by incorporating differentiable forward kinematics, eliminating the reliance on costly motion capture systems. Finally, in the policy fine-tuning stage, we directly fine-tune the policy via backpropagated model gradients, achieving high data efficiency. Through physical validation on the Unitree G1 robot, we demonstrate that HumanoidNDM enables rapid real-world adaptation to various perturbations, representing the first online, MoCap-free fine-tuning framework for humanoid tracking policies.

papers.title: Bug Severity Classification with Fine-Tuned Open LLMs: A Paired Comparison with TF-IDF and CodeBERT Baselines on Eclipse Reports
papers.abstract: Open large language models (LLMs) small enough to run on a laptop are an obvious candidate for automatic bug severity prediction. We measure what they add over cheaper classifiers on one task: assigning one of four Bugzilla severity levels (Critical, Major, Minor, Trivial) to Eclipse bug reports. From a public dump of 361,006 unique Eclipse reports we draw a class-balanced sample of 20,000 rows and compare eleven configurations of nine model types: six TF-IDF classifiers, a fine-tuned CodeBERT encoder, and Llama 3 8B and Qwen 2.5 7B, each run zero-shot and after QLoRA fine-tuning. All eleven are scored on the same 2,000 held-out reports, with bootstrap intervals and McNemar tests. The zero-shot runs reach macro-F1 0.305 and 0.321, below every TF-IDF model (0.430-0.489). The fine-tuned runs reach 0.526 and 0.485, but the zero-shot and fine-tuned setups also differ in checkpoint, serving runtime and decoding, so this gap cannot be credited to fine-tuning alone. Fine-tuned Llama 3 shows no detectable difference from CodeBERT (0.518; difference +0.007, 95% CI -0.017 to +0.032), and fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 is below it on macro-F1. The models differ more by class than in aggregate: fine-tuned Llama 3 finds 36% of Critical reports, Qwen 2.5 finds 69% but only 21% of Minor ones. The dump repeats 60,000 rows, and 8% of the test reports duplicate a training report; removing them lowers TF-IDF scores by up to 0.031 and leaves the LLMs almost unchanged. We release split identifiers, per-report predictions and the analysis script at https://github.com/tbayan/bug_finetuning_llm_artifacts, together with CyberTriage, a tool that serves the fine-tuned classifier locally.

papers.title: Semantic-Coupled Perception Framework for Autonomous Laparoscope Control
papers.abstract: In minimally invasive surgery (MIS), maintaining an appropriate field of view (FoV) is essential for surgical safety and efficiency. However, conventional autonomous laparoscope control methods often treat visual tracking and surgical phase recognition independently, limiting robustness under occlusion, entity overlap, and camera motion. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous laparoscope control framework that couples real-time surgical phase recognition with camera-motion-compensated visual perception. By exploiting phase-dependent relationships among surgical entities, the framework improves target state estimation under challenging visual conditions, supporting task-aware autonomous FoV control. Experiments on benchmark datasets evaluate the proposed framework in surgical phase recognition and target tracking, including scenarios involving occlusion and entity overlap. Phantom experiments further demonstrate the feasibility of autonomous FoV control, showing improved target visibility and task execution performance compared with fixed-FoV control. These results highlight the potential of incorporating task-level semantics into visual state estimation for autonomous laparoscope guidance.

papers.title: Lie symmetry analysis of the Saint--Venant equations with variable bottom
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to apply Lie-symmetry methods to the one-dimensional Saint--Venant shallow-water equations over variable bottom topography. We classify the bottom profiles that admit symmetry extensions, derive similarity reductions to ordinary differential equations, and analyze selected reduced systems. In particular, heteroclinic trajectories yield physically meaningful self-similar solutions describing the draining and filling of water over a quadratic bottom with a fixed shoreline.

papers.title: StickFigure: Enabling Pose-Only IoT Cameras for Privacy-Preserving Edge Vision
papers.abstract: Indoor IoT cameras can support assisted living and activity-aware spaces, but exporting raw RGB frames raises privacy concerns by exposing facial, clothing, and household details that body-motion tasks often do not require. We present StickFigure, a pose-only IoT camera system that, during real-time monitoring, keeps raw frames local and ephemeral while exporting only compact skeleton streams sufficient for downstream human activity recognition (HAR). While pose estimation has matured on GPUs, extracting accurate pose streams on resource-constrained IoT cameras remains difficult. To overcome these challenges and enable on-device pose streams on (almost) any IoT camera, we present two core designs in StickFigure: an activation-aware pose backbone that allocates channel capacity after spatial downsampling and a lightweight hierarchical MLP refiner that selectively corrects elbow and wrist coordinates using intermediate visual features and kinematic context. We fully implement StickFigure and evaluate it on public benchmarks and real-world deployment. Compared with state-of-the-art MCU pose models, StickFigure achieves the highest pose accuracy and downstream HAR utility on both NTU RGB+D and Penn Action, while using 96.5% fewer parameters and 99.3% fewer MACs per frame than RTMPose-S-based baselines, achieving 0.107 s p95 latency on a representative STM32H753 MCU. We believe StickFigure establishes a new operating point for privacy-aware edge vision on massive IoT cameras.

papers.title: AGENS: Agentic Link Construction for Environment and Intent Aware 6G Communication
papers.abstract: The emergence of diverse intelligent services is driving 6G networks toward an intelligent communication ecosystem with increasingly complex operating scenarios. However, existing AI-based communication methods mainly focus on isolated tasks or individual physical-layer mod- ules, which is insufficient for AI-native 6G systems that must jointly perceive dynamic environments, understand specific user intents, coordinate multiple coupled PHY-layer modules, and remain compatible with existing communication infrastructures. To address this gap, this paper, for the first time, explores auto- matic environment- and intent-aware full-link construction, which aims to generate executable PHY-layer configurations according to channel conditions and service requirements. We propose AGENS, an agentic communication decision-making framework for AI-native 6G link construction. Rather than replacing the existing PHY-layer protocol stack with a black-box end-to-end model, AGENS operates on top of the modular communication framework and jointly optimizes end-to-end PHY-layer configu- rations. Specifically, AGENS encodes CSI and natural-language user instructions, aligns communication states with user intents through cross-modal fusion, and leverages a pretrained LLM for intent-aware reasoning. An LSTM-based sequential action generator further captures dependencies among coupled sub- actions and produces structured full-link strategies. To enable stable training in the high-dimensional discrete action space, AGENS adopts a two-stage learning framework, where heuristic supervised initialization is followed by multi-objective reinforce- ment learning to jointly optimize reliability, throughput, and power consumption.

papers.title: Refined analysis on finite-time singularities of almost-holomorphic harmonic map flow
papers.abstract: Building on the work of Song--Waldron~\cite{SongWaldron2024}, we establish stronger regularity and refined blow-up analysis results for almost-holomorphic harmonic map flow from a closed surface into a compact Kähler manifold with nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature. At each finite-time singularity, we improve the outer energy scale to $O((T-t)/\sqrt{|\ln(T-t)|})$. We also prove that both the stress-energy tensor and the tension field converge strongly in $L^2$ to those of the body map, by ruling out concentration of their $L^2$ energy near the singular points. Consequently, the body map belongs to $W^{2,2}$. Finally, an explicit gap theorem for the antiholomorphic energy of nonholomorphic harmonic spheres yields an explicit admissible threshold for the initial antiholomorphic energy under which these conclusions hold.

papers.title: Smart charging without rebound peaks: Wholesale price feedback limits distribution grid peaks from price-responsive electric vehicles
papers.abstract: Studies on price-optimized EV charging consistently find that the common price signal synchronizes charging of the entire fleet of cars in the cheapest hours and creates new "rebound" load peaks in low-voltage grids. Almost all of these studies treat wholesale prices as exogenous, i.e., unaffected by the shifting EV load. This paper argues that this assumption overstates the problem: charging in low-price hours raises the wholesale price in those hours, which spreads charging across hours in equilibrium. I simulate price-optimized charging under real-time prices calibrated to German 2025 data. Even when adjusting for the increase in electricity demand, the coincident import peak of the local grid rises by 260%. After adding a model of equilibrium wholesale prices that takes the price-quantity feedback into account, the increase is reduced to a mere 5%. Allowing for vehicle-to-grid, the export peak rises by 115% under exogenous prices and falls by 6% under endogenous prices. The result holds across vehicle and charging parameters, charging constraints, renewable scenarios, network charges, price functions, peak measures, and simulation assumptions. Rebound peaks remain possible where vehicle adoption runs ahead of the national average or where charging power is high, but they are much smaller than the literature consensus suggests.

papers.title: On the Isoperimetric Inequality for the Third Robin Eigenvalue on Surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate the third Robin eigenvalue on simply connected domains of area $A$ in surfaces with Gaussian curvature bounded above by $K$. For $K>0$, we discover a transition at the critical parameter $α=-4π+KA$: two equal geodesic disks give a sharp upper bound when $α=-4π$ or $-4π+KA\leqα\leq4π$, but the two disk bound fails for $-4π<α<-4π+KA$. In the latter range, we establish a new upper bound involving a single geodesic disk with a modified Robin parameter and prove its sharpness in an explicit subrange. The sharp two-disk inequality persists for nonpositive curvature bounds, and Steklov--Helmholtz analogues are also obtained. Both the two-disk and one-disk bounds arise from a unified two-pole Green-function method, with the one-disk regime emerging from a degenerate area split that produces the $2π$ shift in the effective Robin parameter, while sharpness in the stated subrange is established by boundary oscillations that redistribute Robin boundary mass.

papers.title: Environment-Adaptive Dynamic KV Cache for Multi-Path Parameter Prediction
papers.abstract: Multipath parameter prediction provides a structured and physically interpretable representation of wireless propagation for environment-aware communication systems. However, existing Transformer-based methods repeatedly encode the same environment when predicting multiple BS--UE links, resulting in redundant computation. To address this issue, we propose an environment-conditioned dynamic KV caching framework for multipath parameter prediction. Specifically, we decouple environment-dependent computation from BS--UE geometry, enabling environment-side representations and intermediate KV states to be reused across multiple link queries while only the geometry branch is updated. Building on this reusable cache, we further introduce a dynamic compression mechanism that uses environment-side attention scores to retain informative tokens and adaptively allocates a fixed cache budget across Transformer layers. Experiments on the WAIR-D dataset show that the proposed method reduces KV memory from 0.2500 MB to 0.1406 MB, while the delay NMSE increases only slightly from 0.0673 to 0.0678. Code is available at https://github.com/LZhaoyang/kv.

papers.title: Hydrodynamics for hypersingular interactions by $Γ$-convergence of gradient flows
papers.abstract: We consider the dynamics of $N$ particles with Riesz repulsive interaction in one dimension, focusing in particular on the hypersingular case (i.e. inverse power with power larger than or equal to the dimension). We prove convergence of the empirical measure to the solution of a porous medium equation by the method of $Γ$-convergence of gradient flows introduced by Sandier and the second author. This improves on the prior convergence result by Oelschläger obtained under more stringent assumptions. The method also works for the case where the power is smaller than the dimension, as well as for a class of convex short-range interactions. The proof highlights the crucial role played by the convexity of the interaction, which allows one to show that no excess energy can arise along the flow, implying the needed "slope inequality".

papers.title: Self-Evolution Reasoner: Continuous Optimization via Policy-Intrinsic Exploration and Exploitation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) enables large language models (LLMs) to continuously self-improve their reasoning capabilities. Compared to RLVR's scalar rewards, recent self-supervised on-policy distillation methods leverage denser supervision signals. However, both paradigms suffer from exploration bottlenecks, struggling to escape local optima when the policy fails to sample valid solutions. Relying on external demonstrations can bypass this issue; however, the off-policy nature hinders genuine self-improvement and the mismatched-distribution reasoning can not be fully exploited. In this work, we propose Self-Evolution Policy Optimization (SEPO), a framework that drives continuous reasoning capability evolution via guided exploration and in-distribution exploitation. Specifically, SEPO utilizes labels to elicit correct reasoning from the policy, unlocking the exploration potential. By treating current policy conditioned on this in-distribution reasoning as a self-teacher, SEPO distills the newly discovered solution back into the policy. Through this iterative cycle of policy-intrinsic exploration and exploitation, SEPO achieves robust and continuous capability evolution. Across scientific, tool-use, and complex logical reasoning domains, SEPO consistently achieves the best performance under identical training time or steps, demonstrating superior efficiency and convergence ceilings. Notably, SEPO maintains stable improvements even in scenarios where baselines severely underperform or fail entirely, such as on complex tasks or with small-scale models. Our code is available at https://github.com/Eric8932/SEPO.

papers.title: Spectral localizer for unbounded topological Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: In a series of joint papers with Loring, it was shown how index parings of $K$-theory classes with Fredholm modules can be computed as the half-signature of a suitably constructed finite-dimensional matrix, called the spectral localizer. After offering a novel perspective on earlier results, it is shown how the framework can be extended to unbounded gapped Hamiltonians given as second-order linear differential operators (in particular, matrix-valued Schrödinger and regularized Dirac operators). Important insights are the coercive phase space localization and discretizations by means of wavelets.

papers.title: Convergence Analysis of Variable-Separation-Based Model Reduction for Linear Parametric Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes the convergence of a variable-separation (VS) model reduction method that successively constructs separated approximations to the solutions of linear parametric partial differential equations (PDEs) by solving residual problems at sampled parameter values. We prove that the resulting VS approximations converge almost surely to the exact parametric solution in the parameter-averaged energy norm, under finite-dimensional approximation conditions on the error family and the assumptions of symmetry, uniform coercivity, and uniform boundedness of the governing bilinear forms. For parametric PDEs whose operators and right-hand sides admit finite-term separated representations, we construct finite-dimensional approximation spaces for the error family and bound their dimensions and approximation errors, thereby verifying these approximation conditions and obtaining an $O((\log N)^{-1})$ upper bound for the expected parameter-averaged error energy after $N$ iterations. When the solution families are contained in a fixed finite-dimensional space, we obtain the sharper $O(N^{-1})$ bound for the expected error energy and, if the operator is also parameter-independent, exact recovery for almost every parameter after an almost surely finite number of iterations. Numerical experiments illustrate the error decay of the VS approximations, as well as finite-step recovery in the parameter-independent case.

papers.title: Decoupled Prune-and-Reconstruct: Training on a Compact Core with Double-Layer Sparsification
papers.abstract: On million-node graphs, the memory wall arrives before the compute wall: a GNN that never fits in VRAM cannot deliver the all-node inference its accuracy promises. The standard remedy, pruning, has always been an accuracy tax - paid once and never refunded. DPR refuses this framing. Its central insight is that the mask that shrinks training can also scaffold recovery: one compact node set bounds both computations of graph learning, serving as the encoder's training graph and, at inference, as the anchor from which a sparse structure-aware decoder rebuilds every pruned node (double-layer sparsification). The order is inverted - prune for efficiency, then reconstruct for accuracy - and the tax is repaid: the deployed 30%-budget model trains in 1,450 MiB of peak memory on one 6 GB GPU and recovers 96.9% of its dense-reconstruction reference, beating a same-GPU rerun of the edge-sparsification baseline DSpar by +1.36 pp at 50.1% lower peak training memory; against the same-protocol full-batch no-prune encoder the deployed point pays a measured 2.64 pp accuracy tax for a 2.8x smaller training footprint. Pruning without reconstruction leaves the encoder at 0.378 within the same 40-epoch window (Fig. 4), and all-node serving runs 46x faster than sampling-based GraphSAGE, giving up approx. 5.4 pp of test accuracy. The framework scales to a 2.45M-node production graph at 6,285 MiB of peak training memory; extended variants (long-range context, external text features, a CAN-bus application) are reported as extensions and do not compete with the deployed method, and the 41.8%-budget M4 point, scored on a coarsened super-node graph with its own split, is reported separately rather than compared with the original-node baselines. DPR thus turns aggressive node pruning from an accuracy tax into a safe training accelerator for VRAM-limited all-node inference.

papers.title: SpeC2Rust: Specification-Driven Repository-Level C-to-Rust Translation
papers.abstract: Legacy C codebases remain central to system software and performance-critical infrastructure, but their weak memory safety imposes security and maintenance risks. Recent C-to-Rust translation systems, including LLM-based translators, make automated migration increasingly feasible, yet they still struggle to recover repository-level intent, avoid raw pointers and unsafe constructs, maintain cross-file interfaces, and repair compilation and validation failures efficiently. We propose SpeC2Rust, a specification-driven pipeline for repository-level C-to-Rust translation. It has three stages: (1) Project-Intent Structuring, which decomposes a C repository into semantically coherent modules and generates persistent repository- and module-level specifications; (2) Spec-Guided Generation, which translates each Rust module against these specifications with a live symbol registry to preserve cross-file consistency; and (3) Layered-Feedback Repair, which batches repairs and injects only failure-relevant diagnostics, specification context, and source evidence for efficient compilation and test-driven correction. We evaluate SpeC2Rust on eight repository-level C projects. It generates Rust projects that compile and pass the original end-to-end tests, with no raw-pointer declarations, raw-pointer dereferences, or unsafe lines. On projects shared with an LLM-based baseline, SpeC2Rust reduces cost by 66.1% and input-token usage by 84.7%.

papers.title: Early Selection of Polar Ensemble Decoding with Successive Cancellation Style Component Decoder
papers.abstract: Parallel ensembles of successive cancellation (SC)-style decoders improve error-rate performance by decoding multiple representations of the received vector. Conventional ensembles, however, keep every member active until completion. To reduce computational cost while retaining the diversity gain of ensemble decoding, we propose early ensemble selection (EES), which ranks members using intermediate decoding states and retains a prescribed numbers of members at each predefined selection stage. Within the EES framework, we propose two selection rules, namely path-metric-based selection (PM-EES) and neural-network-based selection (NN-EES). We analytically characterize the computational cost of EES through stage-dependent decoder log-likelihood ratio (LLR) update counts and provide an information-theoretically motivated criterion for choosing selection stages. Simulations on the \((128,64)\) extended BCH code and the \(\operatorname{RM}(4,8)\) code show that suitable selection schedules approach full-ensemble error-rate performance with fewer decoder LLR updates.

papers.title: Feasibility of Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing: From Quantum Links to Algorithms
papers.abstract: Practical fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a large number of physical qubits, posing a major challenge for scaling up individual quantum processors. Distributed architectures offer a promising solution by interconnecting multiple processors through quantum networks. However, remote Bell-pair generation remains technically demanding, making it essential to assess computational performance under limited communication resources. In this work, we present a comprehensive resource analysis of distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation using superconducting processors connected by microwave or optical links. We show that even a single physical communication channel per node can substantially reduce the physical-qubit requirements per node under experimentally motivated, forward-looking microwave-link assumptions of a 1 MHz physical Bell-pair generation rate and 90% fidelity, although at the cost of a roughly tenfold increase in execution time. Conversely, reducing the execution-time overhead requires substantially greater communication resources, including higher Bell-pair fidelities and extensive multiplexing. These results demonstrate the potential feasibility of distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation with limited communication resources and provide a quantitative basis for balancing quantum-link performance, processor size, and execution time.

papers.title: Reversion, Retention, and Semantic Intervention: Measuring Functional Content in CLIP Fine-Tuning Deltas
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning adapts pretrained models to new tasks, but identifying which weight changes support the resulting behavior remains difficult. Weight-space interpretability assigns semantic descriptions to these changes, called fine-tuning deltas. Such descriptions leave open how much task performance depends on the identified updates, particularly when other updates can support the same predictions. We address this gap by pairing reversion, which restores selected parameters to their pretrained values, with retention, which keeps only selected fine-tuning updates. We evaluate Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) models on synthetic financial charts, Flowers102, EuroSAT, and FGVCAircraft with ViT-L/14, and on Flowers102 with ViT-B/16, using a shared recipe that tunes the final six visual blocks. Our contributions are threefold. First, attention value-output (VO) updates alone recover 43-87% of the accuracy improvement, although reverting them leaves chart accuracy unchanged. Cross-entropy loss preserves this contrast on Charts and EuroSAT, while correct-class score margins reveal additional contributions. Second, VO weights recover more loss improvement than all ten equally sized, layer-matched random subsets in each setting. VO and multilayer perceptron (MLP) retentions jointly correct 25-81% of pretrained errors, demonstrating overlapping recovered behavior, which we call operational redundancy. Third, removing semantically selected directions reduces VO-retained recovery more than matched-random removal in all five settings. Together, these results distinguish semantic alignment, removal cost, and retained recovery as complementary evidence about the functional role of fine-tuning updates within the evaluated CLIP recipe.

papers.title: K-energy for the coupled constant scalar curvature Kähler equation, I: Slope formula and semistability
papers.abstract: In this paper we study coupled constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics defined by Datar-Pingali extending coupled Kähler-Einstein metrics defined by Hultgren-Witt Nyström. We consider two K-energy functionals of which one (denoted $\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ccscK}}$) integrates the moment map considered by Datar-Pingali and the other (denoted $\mathcal{M}'$) is designed so that its slope at infinity for subgeodesic rays for ample test configurations with reduced central fiber coincides with the Donaldson-Futaki invariant considered by Hultgren-Witt Nyström and Datar-Pingali. We also extend $\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ccscK}}$ to $\mathcal{H}^{1,\bar{1}}$ and the finite energy class $\mathcal{E}^1$, and prove its convexity along tuples of weak geodesics and finite energy geodesics, respectively. As a corollary, we obtain a semistability condition necessary for the existence of ccscK metrics.

papers.title: Rethinking Retrieval in the Long-Context Era: Training-Free Semantic Trees for Adaptive Context Construction
papers.abstract: Long-context language models can increasingly process entire documents, making full-context prompting a practical alternative to passage retrieval. However, greater capacity determines how much information a model can receive, but not which information best supports a query. This distinction motivates rethinking retrieval: when the full document already fits, can selecting and organizing its evidence improve answering? The challenge is to retain supporting facts and relations while keeping the context focused on the question. To reconcile these goals, we introduce \ours, a training-free framework that uses semantic abstraction to guide selection while retaining original text for answering. \ours constructs a reusable semantic hierarchy from the full document in a single generation, linking node descriptions to source spans. Given a query, structural--semantic scoring and fine-grained lexical attribution nominate shared source nodes; their union with ancestor context preserves structural relations and complete local text. Across four frontier answer models, \ours improves average QA-F1 by 1.72 points over full-context prompting on three LongBench tasks, surpassing the evaluated baselines on the four-model average while reducing answer-context length by 58.55\%. Our code is available at the $\href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/treefuse-ECFE}{repository}$.

papers.title: PS-DLO: Property- and Spatially Aware Deformable Linear Object Manipulation Policy
papers.abstract: Deformable linear objects (DLO) pose a coupled perception and control challenge: their slender geometry makes precise localization difficult, while their deformations depend on object-specific physical properties. To address this challenge, we propose PS-DLO, a property- and spatially aware DLO manipulation policy. First, contrastive image-text learning maps the initial observation to categorical descriptions of DLO properties, providing explicit physical and structural priors for action generation. Second, SAM3 extracts mask-guided features from future observations, which are distilled into the policy's action expert to encode task-relevant DLO regions and their subsequent configurations. We evaluate PS-DLO on nine real-world tasks across single-arm and bimanual platforms, training a shared multi-task policy for each embodiment. PS-DLO achieves an average success rate of 68.9%, exceeding the strongest baseline by 20.0 percentage points. In generalization experiments, PS-DLO achieves higher success rates than the baseline in six of seven visual-shift conditions on butterfly-knot untying. These results demonstrate that combining object-property priors with future spatial supervision improves multi-task DLO manipulation and robustness to visual variation.

papers.title: MuSTEL: A Large-Scale Multilingual Synthetic Text-Line Image Dataset for OCR
papers.abstract: Optical character recognition (OCR) systems depend strongly on the scale and diversity of their training data. One approach to document OCR first analyzes the page layout and extracts text-line images, which are then transcribed by a recognition model. Multilingual line-level recognition involving Persian, Arabic, and English presents additional challenges because different writing directions, fonts, and styles may coexist within a single line. This paper introduces MuSTEL, a large-scale synthetic multilingual OCR dataset containing more than 14.5 million annotated text-line images, organized into a training partition and predefined small and large test sets. Samples are generated from natural-language corpora, including multilingual content already present in the source texts. The generation framework incorporates capability-aware font selection, within-line font and style changes, mixed-direction text rendering, highlighting, and underlining. A validated repository of 2,009 font files from 711 families supports broad typographic coverage, while varied backgrounds, blur, geometric distortion, skew, stroke width, and image save quality provide diverse document-like appearances. Statistical analysis characterizes the dataset's language composition, transcription lengths, lexical and character-sequence diversity, image dimensions, typography, and rendering conditions. MuSTEL provides a resource for training and evaluating multilingual line-level OCR systems and investigating recognition robustness across languages, writing directions, and visual conditions.

papers.title: Humans in Space: Can MLLMs Construct Human-Centric Spatial Understanding via Active Exocentric Exploration?
papers.abstract: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) excel at zero-shot reasoning, their spatial capabilities are primarily evaluated through static, passive observation. In complex, human-centric scenes, occlusion often hides crucial geometric evidence, and passive benchmarks force models to guess rather than recognize their own visual uncertainty. To bridge this gap, we introduce SATE-Bench, a novel interactive benchmark comprising 316 real-world scenes and 2,525 multi-turn QA pairs to evaluate visual self-awareness and active exocentric view-exploration. It combines a Passive multi-view control with an Active exploration setting, where models start from a severely occluded view and must iteratively query adjacent viewpoints until they gather enough evidence to fully ``sate'' the question, scored by a step-penalized efficiency reward. Evaluating state-of-the-art MLLMs reveals that they terminate exploration prematurely while reporting high confidence, and struggle with fine-grained 3D geometric tasks; matched-view controls further attribute the Active--Passive gap primarily to insufficient evidence acquisition. Moreover, fine-tuning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) shows that rewarding view-seeking increases active exploration but lowers overall accuracy, as models over-explore and fail to fuse expanding multi-view contexts across turns. These findings indicate that scaling passive multi-view perception does not intrinsically yield active spatial reasoning, highlighting the need for models that know where to look, how to integrate what they see, and when to stop. Code and data are available at https://gtc-gh.github.io/SATE-Bench/

papers.title: Uncovering Latent Patterns in Program-Associated Library Attendance through Background Adjustment
papers.abstract: Routinely collected library entrance records offer an opportunity to understand attendance patterns associated with library programs, but ordinary daily variation and detailed administrative user status categories complicate their interpretation. Building on a project-based learning collaboration with Kyushu University Central Library, we analyzed entrance records from October 2018 to July 2026. Descriptive analysis revealed relatively modest differences in attendance across the main weather categories, higher attendance on days with mean temperatures of 30°C or above, and pronounced differences between weekdays and weekends. To account for such background variation, we estimated expected attendance for each user status category and applied nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) to identify common patterns in positive background-adjusted responses from 92 events across 39 user status categories. Three interpretable response modes were identified: two concentrated on temporary external visitors and undergraduates, respectively, and one representing a broader combination of graduate student and research-related categories. The three-mode solution was selected by jointly considering held-out reconstruction error and basis stability across year-excluded fits. The identified modes also remained stable after excluding events from the selected COVID-19 period. The modes appeared in different combinations across individual events, with their dominance varying by program category. These findings illustrate how existing library records can reveal interpretable patterns of program-associated attendance without predefined grouping of user status categories.

papers.title: Execution Logs Sway VLM Judges of Robot Progress
papers.abstract: Vision-language models now grade robot videos, and text placed beside the frames can change their verdicts. On clips where the robot is losing progress, we add one log line saying the robot is making progress. Across Gemini, Qwen and GPT judges, this flips correct verdicts to progress 10 to 35 percentage points more often than a neutral line does. A one-line warning that the log may be wrong removes most of this effect. Selected fake "task complete" claims flip half of Qwen's correct verdicts, against a tenth for unrelated log lines. They have no detectable effect on Gemini.

papers.title: Well located Banach spaces - A combined approach to L_1- preduals and Hilbert space
papers.abstract: In the description of L_1- preduals on the one hand and of Hilbert spaces, on the other, one encounters the surprising appearance of similar classes of operators in terms of their extendibility properties in the setting of these two classes of spaces. It also turns out that the extension properties are closely tied to how the two classes of spaces are positioned inside the ambient spaces. It is well known that in the case of all subspaces being positioned inside a larger space Z as a complemented subspace leads to Z being (isomorphically) a Hilbert space whereas in the case of a Banach space X which is complemented inside all its superspaces, it turns out that X is an injective Banach space. In this paper, we shall be concerned mostly with such properties as demanding that X sit inside the ambient space as a locally complemented subspace (and sometimes as a Lipchitz retract). It turns out that the class of Banach spaces X determined by the indicated properties are precisely the class of L_1- preduals in the former case and of Hilbert spaces, in the latter. As an important consequence of this approach, we are led to several new characterisations of Hilbert spaces in terms of the extendibility of bounded linear maps coming from well-known operator (nonlinear operator) ideals.

papers.title: Certifying Reward Alignment in Portfolio Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Financial reinforcement learning often translates an investment objective into an additive risk-adjusted reward. An agent can optimise that reward accurately yet implement a different financial preference. We develop a decision audit for terminal mean-variance equilibrium that separates reward misspecification from learning error. In a finite exogenous-state market, we bound the gain from changing one action using actor, reward and continuation-critic residuals. The certificate ignores state-constant critic offsets, accommodates convex action constraints, and has an independent-sample extension that does not require the equilibrium policy. A continuation-aware actor-critic method estimates the future-policy correction from samples. Across nine controlled markets and twenty seeds, it reduces policy distance by and one-step deviation gain by relative to a matched myopic-reward network. A separate PPO comparison tests the same reward intervention within a standard optimiser. Historical tests cross seven covariance estimators and 10, 30 and 49 US industry portfolios over 432 months: joint reward calibration preserves each fitted mean-variance target, but does not improve realised investment performance. Together, these results provide a way to quantify whether a learned decision implements its stated financial objective, separately from how well that objective performs in a backtest.

papers.title: Edge-Centric Adaptive Neural Activation via Parametric Tanh Functions
papers.abstract: Within the broader landscape of artificial intelligence architectures, this paper introduces a compact, edge-centric neural framework that resolves the computational bottlenecks of modern edge-activated paradigms like Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) while retaining their expressiveness over traditional Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs). While KANs demonstrate remarkable representational capacity by placing learnable univariate functions on connection edges rather than hidden nodes, their reliance on non-local B-splines introduces severe optimization hurdles, high memory overhead, and poor hardware scaling. To bridge this gap, we propose the Parametric Tanh Connection Function, a smooth, bounded architectural primitive defined as $a_{\tanh}(x;δ,α,β,γ) = δ+ α\tanh(βx + γ)$. This formulation unifies offset, amplitude, local slope, and horizontal displacement into a lightweight, 4-parameter differentiable mapping optimized edge-by-edge via backpropagation. Evaluated on dense architectures using MNIST and CIFAR-10, our parametric tanh connection model achieves significant absolute accuracy gains over traditional affine baselines-reaching 95.63% $\pm$ 0.08% on MNIST and 44.74% $\pm$ 0.18% on CIFAR-10. Crucially, it matches or exceeds the expressiveness of unconstrained 7-parameter exponential connection baselines while requiring up to 85% less training runtime. By replacing complex splines or hyper-flexible exponents with a bounded, analytically smooth hyperbolic tangent kernel, this work delivers a highly scalable, hardware-friendly compromise for heterogeneous connection-level deep learning.

papers.title: Colored Partitions and Minimal Excludants
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce the concept of minimal excludants in colored partitions and extend it to the framework of least $r$-gaps. In particular, we focus on $k$-colored partitions and cubic partitions, deriving the generating functions for the sums of minimal excludants and least $r$-gaps, and analyzing their asymptotic behaviors. Notably, the presented theory is comprehensively extended by the systematic generalization of each result for minimal excludants in $k$-colored partitions to the case of least $r$-gaps. We introduce generalized cubic partitions and discover the minimal excludant, as well as several additional results.

papers.title: ASR-Protected Fusion and Reference-Anchored Policy Optimization for Joint ASR and Word-Level Speech Anti-Spoofing
papers.abstract: Existing anti-spoofing systems report either an utterance-level score or a time-based spoof interval: the former cannot show which words are spoofed, while the latter does not directly match the transcript and must be post-aligned with words, so alignment errors can lead to wrong word-level labels. Standard ASR model outputs only text; spoof information in the audio is lost after recognition and is not passed with the transcript. Yet changing only a few words can change the meaning of a sentence, leaving downstream systems to use incorrect text without knowing which words are spoofed. We therefore treat partial anti-spoofing as tagged ASR: the model transcribes speech and marks spoofed words at the same time, directly linking spoof labels to output words. We adopt the audio LLM and use ASR-Protected Subspace Gated Fusion (APSGF) to fuse spoof cues with ASR features. Spoof cues are added only outside an ASR-protected subspace, so they do not disturb recognition features. After cross-entropy training, we fine-tune the model with Reference-Anchored Policy Optimization (RAPO). Since the SFT policy is already concentrated, multiple samples from the same input tend to receive similar rewards, resulting in weak group-wise advantages. RAPO instead generates a single sample with low sampling randomness and anchors its advantage to the reward of a reference model. This allows the model to reinforce responses that outperform the reference while suppressing those that underperform it. Experiments on five datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in jointly detecting spoofed words and preserving ASR accuracy. The code is publicly available.

papers.title: LoopGR: Parameter-Efficient Scaling for Generative Recommendation via Recurrent Depth
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation formulates item recommendation as autoregressive generation rather than a discriminative scoring problem. Although empirical studies exhibit favorable scaling behavior in recommendation, unleashing the benefits of scaling remains challenging under the strict model size and inference cost constraints of real-world systems. A central challenge is to combine expressive modeling of user-item interaction histories with flexible computational depth without proportionally increasing model size. We introduce LoopGR, a parameter-efficient scaling framework for generative recommendation via recurrent depth. LoopGR employs a tailored hierarchical recurrent depth mechanism that alternates between a shared generative decoder and a lightweight context updater. For efficient inference, we further develop recurrent trajectory self-distillation that distills a low-budget student from a high-budget teacher by aligning both predictive distributions and evolution directions. Extensive experiments show that LoopGR consistently outperforms strong generative recommendation baselines. Compared with a representative encoder-decoder baseline, LoopGR achieves superior performance while reducing model size by up to 52%. These results establish recurrent depth as a new scaling dimension, offering a flexible and resource-efficient scaling path for generative recommendation.

papers.title: Last-Iterate Stationarity of Muon with Finitely Many Newton-Schulz Iterations
papers.abstract: Muon has demonstrated strong empirical performance in large-scale language-model training, motivating a deeper theoretical understanding of its practical implementation. Unlike the idealized polar-factor update, practical Muon employs a fixed number of quintic Newton-Schulz iterations. Existing analyses primarily establish average- or best-iterate stationarity guarantees, while last-iterate convergence remains less understood. In this work, we investigate last-iterate gradient convergence of practical finite-step Muon on smooth, lower-bounded nonconvex objectives. In the deterministic setting, we show that Muon without input stabilization can exhibit cyclic behavior even on a smooth convex quadratic. In contrast, with positive stabilization, we establish last-iterate gradient convergence and square-summability of gradients for any fixed momentum coefficient below one and a sufficiently small constant learning rate. In the stochastic setting, we first demonstrate that persistent bounded, unbiased noise can prevent convergence under fixed learning rates and momentum, even with positive stabilization. We then establish almost-sure and mean-square last-iterate gradient convergence under bounded-variance stochastic gradients by combining diminishing learning rates with increasing momentum. Finally, we construct a smooth counterexample demonstrating that neither convergence theorem implies a pointwise polynomial convergence rate. Nevertheless, we establish density-one convergence rates, guaranteeing polynomial gradient decay for all but an asymptotically vanishing fraction of iterations.

papers.title: Single-Cycle Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction with Compressed Continuous Wavelet Features and Deep Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in industrial applications, but their performance gradually degrades over time, making accurate lifetime prediction important for safety and reliability. However, reliable lifetime assessment generally requires extensive degradation testing, which is both costly and time-consuming. To reduce this burden, recent data-driven approaches have sought to predict the end-of-life cycle of batteries from only the initial few cycles. Nevertheless, identifying reliable degradation patterns from such limited early-cycle data remains challenging because early aging dynamics are often subtle and nonlinear. To address this issue, we adopt the continuous wavelet transform to convert cycle-wise voltage, current, and capacity signals into time-frequency representations, enabling multi-resolution characterization of degradation behavior. Building on this representation, we apply scale compression to reduce redundancy while preserving structural information in the scalograms. We evaluate the proposed framework on eight benchmark datasets derived from seven public battery datasets covering diverse electrode chemistries, cell form factors, and cycling protocols. Experimental results show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms prior approaches in single-cycle remaining useful life prediction and remains robust as the number of input cycles increases from 1 to 100. In addition, redundancy-fidelity analysis characterizes the trade-off introduced by scale compression, and gradient-based visual explanations indicate that the model focuses on localized time-frequency regions associated with structured signal transitions during charge-discharge operation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed framework for early-cycle battery remaining useful life prediction.

papers.title: Finite-sum Identities and Supercongruences for Cubes of Catalan Numbers
papers.abstract: Let $C_k=\binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ be the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $p$ be an odd prime. We establish exact finite-sum identities that, together with known binomial supercongruences and reductions of Sun, yield $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{16^k}\equiv2-24y^2-\frac{5p^2}{2y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{(-8)^k}\equiv-1-48y^2-\frac{33p^2}{16y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+4y^2\equiv1\pmod4$. We also evaluate the corresponding sum with denominator $16^k(k+1)^2$, and obtain two weighted Catalan supercongruences. The finite identities follow from the ratios of consecutive summands, symmetry of double sums, and telescoping. All endpoint terms are retained over the rational numbers before any modular reduction. In each bilinear identity, one endpoint denominator equals $p$; its cancellation produces the necessary term of order $p^2$. The precise arithmetic inputs are stated separately.

papers.title: Modelling Emotional Dynamics in the Life of Amrita Pritam: A Nonlinear Perspective on Longing and Companionship
papers.abstract: Amrita Pritam (1919-2005) was a prominent writer of modern Indian literature, particularly in Punjabi and Hindi. Her literary-biographical context provides a setting for exploring memory, longing, companionship, and emotional regulation through simple dynamical models. This study develops three single-state ordinary differential equation models centred on two important relational references in her life: Sahir Ludhianvi, associated with memory, absence, recollection, and longing, and Imroz, associated with companionship, care, continuity, and support. The first model describes Sahir-related longing through memory-driven excitation and natural emotional decay (fading); the second models Imroz-related companionship through nonlinear stabilisation around a preferred emotional state; and the third unifies both influences within a single-state framework. Analytical solutions, equilibrium conditions, local stability analysis, and numerical simulations are used to examine emotional-state decay and persistence, convergence to stable equilibria, and threshold effects on system behaviour. The results indicate that memory-related reinforcement may sustain the modelled emotional state under suitable stimulus conditions, whereas Imroz-related companionship may drive the system towards a stable upper equilibrium when initial conditions lie within the admissible range. The unified model illustrates how memory-driven longing and companionship-driven stabilisation associated with Sahir and Imroz can jointly shape a modelled emotional trajectory. This study is conceptual and mathematical, not empirical or psychological. It neither measures private emotions of Amrita Pritam nor estimates parameters from biographical data. Instead, it introduces a simple nonlinear framework for exploring memory, fading, companionship, equilibrium, and threshold effects in a literary-biographical context.

papers.title: MMFact: Simplifying Multimodal Misinformation Detection with Shared Resources and Tools
papers.abstract: Multimodal misinformation detection methods often rely on different preprocessing pipelines and auxiliary resources, making experimental comparisons difficult to interpret. We present MMFact, a collection of shared resources and tools that simplifies this research workflow. It brings together 47 detector implementations and baselines, three multimodal datasets, and prepared materials ranging from semantic features to OCR, image descriptions, and external evidence. Compatible methods can use the same materials, reducing variation introduced by preprocessing and supporting fairer comparisons. A modular training and evaluation framework preserves method-specific designs while providing common experimental procedures. By treating prepared materials as a shared research resource, MMFact helps researchers focus on developing and evaluating detection methods.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Crowd Flow Control Using Dynamic Barriers
papers.abstract: Crowd barriers are widely used to regulate pedestrian movement during large public events such as pilgrimages. However, fixed barrier layouts often create unnecessary stopping and local congestion even when they successfully control the overall crowd flow. Finding better barrier configurations is difficult because there is no dataset that provides the best barrier placement for a given crowd scene. We address this challenge by introducing a simulation-driven reinforcement learning framework that learns barrier configurations without requiring labelled training data. Starting from a segmented crowd scene, we construct a realistic simulation environment that reproduces the observed pedestrian distribution. This environment is then used to train a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) agent that continuously adjusts barrier positions to improve pedestrian movement. Unlike supervised approaches the proposed framework allows the agent to explore barrier configurations that have never been observed in real data. We evaluate the learned policy under unseen numbers of pedestrians. The learned policy consistently outperforms the existing manually designed barrier configuration by reducing pedestrian stops while maintaining effective flow regulation. These results demonstrate that combining computer vision crowd simulation and reinforcement learning provides an effective framework for optimizing crowd control infrastructure.

papers.title: Repetitive Magnetic Penrose Process
papers.abstract: The nonlinear iterative repetitive Penrose process established recently by Ruffini et al.\ is generalized to the magnetic Penrose process. The spacetime background is the Kerr metric, the external magnetic field is described by the Wald solution, the electromagnetic field is treated as a test field, and the charge is treated as a test charge. We analyze the optimal conditions for maximum energy extraction on the equatorial plane and find that under these conditions the core mechanism of the iterative process is charging feedback. After charging, the black hole charge is approximately half of the Wald charge. When the neutral parent particle decays, charge conservation forces the infalling fragment to carry charge while the other fragment carries the opposite charge, so the black hole charge accumulates monotonically. The monopole voltage of the Wald solution decreases linearly with the charge $Q$ and crosses zero to reverse sign at a certain point, so the magnetic gain is gradually neutralized by the charge. The repetitive magnetic Penrose process is therefore forced to terminate and eventually falls back to the mechanical Penrose process. The energy extraction efficiency $>100\%$ predicted by the single magnetic Penrose process will therefore be prevented.

papers.title: Population-average trajectories and slopes in smooth random changepoint mixed models
papers.abstract: Two-slope mixed-effects models with subject-specific changepoints are widely used to describe biphasic longitudinal trajectories. Treatment-arm summaries are often reported using a single "typical subject" curve obtained by plugging mean parameter values into the subject-specific model. This can be misleading when changepoint timing varies across individuals, because averaging subject-specific curves is not the same as evaluating one curve at average parameter values. A related issue is that individual trajectories may bend gradually rather than change slope through a literal kink, with transition sharpness varying between subjects. We propose population-average estimands for two-slope mixed models with random changepoints and smooth subject-level transitions. These estimands target the treatment-arm mean trajectory and instantaneous slope by averaging over fitted heterogeneity in changepoint timing and transition sharpness. We use a baseline-anchored normal-convolution soft hinge, which preserves the broken stick interpretation, includes the abrupt changepoint model as a limiting case, and allows analytic evaluation of the changepoint-marginalized kernels under a truncated normal changepoint distribution for fixed transition sharpness. Averaging over the fitted transition sharpness distribution is then performed by deterministic one-dimensional quadrature. In an application to HIV-1 RNA data from ACTG Protocol 315, with censoring and heavy-tailed residuals, the marginal summaries reveal a more gradual population-level transition than conventional plug-in summaries. The marginal slope remains more negative for longer, and the marginal mean continues to decline after the plug-in curve has begun to flatten. These results illustrate the main reporting implication: in random changepoint models, representative subject curves should not be treated as population-average trajectories or slopes.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions of the compressible MHD equations on the half space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the global well-posedness and large-time asymptotic behavior of strong solutions to the $n$-dimensional ($n\ge 2$) compressible viscous resistive magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations in the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}_+^n$. We impose the standard no-slip boundary condition on the velocity field and two types of physically relevant boundary conditions on the magnetic field: the insulating boundary condition and the perfectly conducting boundary condition. Under the assumption that the initial data are small perturbations of the constant equilibrium state $(\barρ, \mathbf{0}, \mathbf{0})$, we first establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions in Sobolev spaces by deriving uniform energy estimates and using a bootstrapping argument. Then, by combining the sharp decay estimates of solutions to the corresponding linearized system with Duhamel's principle, we obtain the decay rates of solutions to the nonlinear problem. Specifically, we prove that the solutions decay at the rate $t^{-\frac{n}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{p}\right)}$ in $L^p$ norm for $2\le p\le\infty$, and we also establish the decay rates of their first-order derivatives. Furthermore, we show that the global solutions converge to the linearized solutions with an improved decay rate as time goes to infinity. Our results extend the classical results of Kagei and Kobayashi \cite{Kagei-Kobayashi2002, Kagei-Kobayashi2005} for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the half space to the compressible MHD system with both insulating and perfectly conducting boundary conditions.

papers.title: Task Success Is Not Enough: Side-effect-Aware Evaluation of Tool-Using Language Model Agents
papers.abstract: Tool-using language model agents are usually evaluated by whether they finish the user's task. That metric misses a common failure: an agent can complete the requested work while also taking an unauthorized side-effecting action, such as writing to the wrong object, expanding the scope of the request, or contacting an unintended recipient. We call this failure mode collateral damage (CD). We introduce SABench (Side-effect-Aware Benchmark), a benchmark of 201 email, calendar, and ticket tasks. Each task crosses one of four state structures (independent, dependent, externally reachable, cross-tool) with one of four trap families (ambiguity, mis-targeting, cascade harm, overreach), and each task has a deterministic trace-based oracle for both goal satisfaction and authorization compliance. Across 2,211 model-task pairs from 11 frontier LLMs spanning major commercial and open model families, 15.2% of all runs incur CD, with risk concentrated in ambiguity tasks (38.8% violation rate) while non-ambiguous traps average 8.4% CD. Among goal-satisfied runs, 12.8% still produce unauthorized writes. Cross-tool and dependent states have about twice the CD rate of independent states. CD rates vary by 4.7x across models at comparable goal rates, which suggests that task success alone is a poor proxy for safe tool use. The SABench task corpus is released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Phaedrus/sabench; the traces, oracle, code, and analysis pipeline are released at https://github.com/hjj194/sabench-artifact.

papers.title: Field misalignment effect on the in-plane magnetoresistance in the high-temperature superconductor FeSe/SrTiO3
papers.abstract: The azimuthal angular dependence of the in-plane magnetoresistance provides a powerful probe for detecting rotational symmetry breaking in superconductors, which has significant implications for understanding the superconducting pairing symmetry and the intertwined orders. However, in two-dimensional or layered superconductors with strong anisotropy between in-plane and out-of-plane critical fields, measuring the in-plane magnetoresistance is particularly challenging as it is extremely sensitive to the field misalignment. Here we perform systematic electrical transport measurements on ultrathin FeSe films grown on SrTiO3 substrates. By remounting the same FeSe film to change the field misalignment, two qualitatively different angular dependences of the in-plane magnetoresistance are observed in the superconducting transition region, indicating the extreme sensitivity of the measurement to field misalignment. The observed anisotropic in-plane magnetoresistance can be well captured by our geometric model considering the field misalignment effect. Our work provides a practical framework for disentangling the misalignment effect and investigating the in-plane rotational symmetry breaking in two-dimensional or layered superconductors.

papers.title: Flexible Beamforming via Fluid Antenna Array: From Discrete to Continuous Array
papers.abstract: Fluid antenna arrays (FAAs) reconfigure their effective aperture by activating radiation ports from a dense set of candidate positions within a finite physical region, thereby offering geometry diversity beyond conventional fixed arrays. This paper studies arbitrary-direction far-field beam synthesis with a planar FAA. Since a fixed array adapts its beamforming weights on a predetermined spatial sampling structure, its ability to match desired beam patterns is limited when both the aperture and the number of active elements are constrained. To exploit the geometry diversity of the FAA, we propose a coarse-to-fine scheme that couples discrete port selection with continuous joint refinement. In the coarse stage, a fast Fourier transform (FFT) based phase retrieval step converts the amplitude-only beam specification into an aperture-compatible complex target, after which an FFT-tailored greedy method selects the active ports and least squares initializes their complex weights. In the fine stage, a projected adaptive moment estimation procedure jointly refines the continuous port positions and beamforming weights while enforcing the minimum interelement spacing. For the evaluated two-beam configuration, the proposed scheme increases the mainlobe energy fraction from 35.73% to 48.92% and reduces the peak sidelobe level from -2.30 dB to -3.83 dB relative to a fixed array with the same aperture and active-port count.

papers.title: Cascaded Posterior Sampling With Diffusion Priors for highly Accelerated MRI
papers.abstract: Diffusion models are powerful priors for inverse problems, including accelerated MRI. However, modeling the distribution of high-resolution images requires large networks with high computational cost. We propose a posterior sampling framework that uses cascaded diffusion models as multiscale priors. Conditioned on a coarse image, the distribution of fine-scale detail is local and well conditioned, and it can therefore be captured by a small network. Similarly, a small unconditional network is sufficient to represent low-resolution images, and it is used to recover the coarse image from the k-space center. This estimate then conditions the high-resolution prior, which is combined with all measurements to recover the final image. Both priors are trained on images alone, so they apply to any sampling pattern, and data consistency remains linear at every scale. In multi-coil brain MRI, the proposed method improves on the best single-scale diffusion baseline by 4-6 dB in PSNR at 15x acceleration, while each of its separately trained networks is about 10x smaller. The gain grows as the problem becomes more ill-posed, and ablations show that it arises from informative low-resolution conditioning.

papers.title: MetaARIMA: Configuration-Level Transfer Learning for ARIMA Models
papers.abstract: Time Series Foundation Models have demonstrated that pretraining on diverse datasets enables effective transfer to new forecasting tasks. Classical methods like ARIMA, however, remain configured and trained independently for each series, discarding knowledge from previous experiments. Consequently, selecting and training an ARIMA configuration remains challenging and often relies on heuristic approaches based on in-sample goodnessof-fit measures. We propose MetaARIMA, a pretrained configuration policy based on metalearning that brings transfer learning to classical statistical forecasting at the configuration level rather than the model level. The policy learns from historical experiments which ARIMA configurations achieve top-quantile performance, and recommends promising candidates for new series while preserving interpretability and local estimation. At inference, it selects a diverse set of candidates via maximal marginal relevance and efficiently identifies the final configuration using successive halving. Experiments in a transfer learning setting, training on M4 and evaluating on M1, M3, and Tourism, show that MetaARIMA outperforms AutoARIMA and other classical methods while being more dataefficient. In a comparison with recent zero-shot foundation models, MetaARIMA remains competitive with Chronos2, Moirai2, and TimesFM. The experiments are publicly available at https://github.com/vcerqueira/experiments-metaarima.

papers.title: Shaping of invariant measures of iterated function systems
papers.abstract: We study an inverse problem for iterated function systems: given maps $w_1,\dots,w_m$ on a Polish space and a target probability measure $ν$, choose the law $μ$ with which the maps are sampled so that the invariant measure $π_μ$ of the resulting Markov chain is as close as possible to $ν$ in the Wasserstein-1 distance. The minimization runs over the admissible set $A$ of sampling laws for which the chain has a unique invariant measure attracting every initial law; the maps need not be contractions. On bounded state spaces, regions certified by a Doeblin or splitting condition are convex unions of relatively open faces of the simplex, and they exhaust $A$ when the state space is finite; for affine systems with nonnegative matrices $A$ is a spectral sublevel set; in general $A$ is neither open, closed, convex nor connected. Existence of an optimal law reduces to the invariant measures left behind at the missing boundary $\mathrm{cl}(A)\setminus A$: boundary points without invariant measures of finite first moment repel minimizing sequences, which yields existence for all systems of homotheties of $\mathbb R^d$, and for compact state spaces a solution exists for every target if and only if the set of reachable invariant measures is closed; a two-state example shows that existence can fail. A search over a $δ$-net returns an $ε$-optimal law over any region on which $μ\mapstoπ_μ$ is Lipschitz and the chains are uniformly attracting, with explicit constants and, on an interval, an explicit sample size. Under contraction on average, $μ\mapstoπ_μ$ is differentiable, its derivative is injective if and only if the push-forwards $(w_i)_\#π_μ$ are linearly independent, and the objective is weakly convex, so that a projected subgradient method with inexact subgradients converges to near-stationary points.

papers.title: Reasoning or Just Prompting? Probing the Mechanism of Latent Chemical Reasoning
papers.abstract: Latent reasoning performs intermediate computation in continuous space rather than through explicit tokens, which is particularly appealing in chemistry, where errors in explicit reasoning can propagate to the final answer. Yet if latent states truly constitute an implicit reasoning chain, they should be causally important. We find otherwise: swapping or moderately perturbing intermediate latent states has little effect on performance, while removing them entirely sometimes causes a substantial score drop. Thus, the latent states matter, but their molecule-specific content appears to matter far less. This points to a simpler interpretation. Rather than encoding a step-by-step reasoning chain, latent states may primarily steer subsequent model computation, much like soft prompts. Indeed, a single fixed prefix shared across molecules reproduces LatentChem's performance, and a learned static soft prompt performs comparably to per-input latent generation in controlled models. The tolerance of latent sequences to substitution and moderate perturbation further supports this connection. We therefore suggest that latent chemical reasoning may be better viewed as soft prompting than as a reasoning chain hidden in continuous space.

papers.title: Time-asymptotic expansion and fluid approximation of the 1D Boltzmann equation with hard potentials
papers.abstract: We establish a quantitative large-time comparison between the macroscopic Boltzmann solution and the full nonlinear compressible Navier-Stokes solution in one space dimension. For Maxwellian molecules and hard potentials with angular cutoff, we consider small, spatially compactly supported perturbations of a global Maxwellian with polynomial velocity decay, without assuming spatial differentiability. Nonlinear diffusion waves persist at leading order, making comparison through linearized equations alone insufficient. We construct a coupled system for the leading nonlinear fluid waves and derive cancellation identities from the exact kinetic spectral representation to control interactions between distinct characteristic families. Combined with a particle-fluid decomposition, these yield pointwise estimates separating the leading waves, their interactions, and a faster-decaying remainder.

papers.title: An efficient method for reconstructing the potential in the fractional Calderón problem with a single measurement
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a numerical method for determining the potential function in one-dimensional and two-dimensional fractional-order Calderón problems through a single measurement. The fractional Laplacian is discretized using the finite difference method, and the POD-RBF method is used to construct the forward problem surrogate model that can provide the predicted value and its exact gradient in time. The inverse problem is solved using Tikhonov regularization and the conjugate gradient method. The efficiency and effectiveness of the developed method are demonstrated through numerical experiments, and the theoretical results are verified.

papers.title: Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation
papers.abstract: We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $θ$ and $η$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response. By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $θ$ and $η$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.

papers.title: Freeze What Is Settled, Cache What Is Smooth: Spatial Freezing Keeps Step Caching in Its Low-Error Regime
papers.abstract: Instruction-based image editors built on diffusion transformers run tens of denoising steps. Training-free acceleration either reuses features across steps (step caching) or stops computing the regions an edit leaves untouched (region freezing), and the two have been combined before. We ask how a high speed-up target should be split between them. On Qwen-Image-2.1, freezing does more than remove tokens: it lowers the cost of every step, so the step cache can reach the same overall speed-up with a conservative threshold that keeps its error small.
